title: How an Electric Motor Works in 60 Seconds ⚡🔄 #shorts
description:
Electric motors use around 45% of all the world's electricity. Inside, a copper coil becomes an electromagnet, magnets push and pull it around, and a commutator flips the current every half turn so it never stops spinning. Push, pull, flip, spin. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#electricmotor #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Motor
steps.text: Electric motors use almost *half* of all the electricity on Earth.

steps.label: Coil & Magnets
steps.text: Inside a simple motor, a *copper* coil sits between two strong magnets.

steps.label: Electromagnet
steps.text: Send current through the coil, and it becomes an *electromagnet*, with its own north and south pole.

steps.label: Push & Pull
steps.text: Like poles push, opposite poles pull. So the coil *twists* toward the magnets.

steps.label: Commutator
steps.text: Just as it lines up, a split ring called the *commutator* flips the current. The poles swap, and it keeps turning.

steps.label: Spin
steps.text: Bigger motors flip the current with *electronics*, spinning fans, trains and electric cars.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Push, pull, flip, *spin*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
